title: Almost plurinodal alteration of the first term of a proper hypercover
statement: Let $S$ and $X$ be integral excellent Noetherian schemes of finite dimension, and let $f:X\to S$ be proper dominant [def-weil-proper-morphism]. There exist an integral excellent Noetherian scheme $T$, an alteration $a:T\to S$, and an augmented proper hypercover $\epsilon:Y_\bullet\to X\times_S T$ such that $Y_0\to T$ is an almost plurinodal datum in the sense of [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Here proper hypercover means that the augmentation in degree zero and all simplicial matching maps are proper surjective. Each $Y_i$ is finite type over $T$, so has a finite bound on its fibre dimensions. Each curve factor of each plurinodal summand comes with a closed subscheme finite over its base containing its nonsmooth locus, as required by the tower data. The semistable tower summands of $Y_0\to T$ have relative dimension equal to the dimension of the generic fibre of $f$; the other summand has nowhere dense image. One may take $\dim T=\dim S$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 and Lemma 3.3.2, pp. 9--10, from de Jong plurinodal alterations. This is an existence statement for the hypercover, not a nearby-cycle theorem. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $K=\kappa(\eta_S)$ and $d=\dim X_K$. The integral generic fibre is of finite type over $K$, so $d$ is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to $X_K$: it gives a finite separable field extension $L/K$ such that every irreducible component of $X_L$ is geometrically irreducible. This is precisely the field extension used at the start of Orgogozo's proof; it asserts geometric irreducibility, not geometric reducedness.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, first sentence of proof, printed p. 9

proof.text: Take the normalization $S_0$ of $S$ in $L$, using [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] at $\eta_S$. Its function field is $L$. It is finite: on an affine integral chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, excellence makes $R$ Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata]; the prime $0$ in [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] say exactly that its integral closure in the finite extension $L/K$ is a finite $R$-module. This is the affine construction specified by the normalization node. The integral map is dominant, so is surjective: its image is closed (finite maps are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]) and contains $\eta_S$. It is an alteration. Its finite-type affine coordinate rings are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], hence Noetherian, and finite over a Noetherian quasi-compact base gives a Noetherian scheme by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension], $\dim S_0=\dim S$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, normalization of S in the finite generic extension; Stacks 035H, 032R, 032F, 07QV, 07QU and 02JX

proof.text: The scheme $X_{S_0}$ is proper over $S_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and excellent by the affine form of [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. It has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Give every component its reduced induced structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The components dominating $S_0$ are the reduced closures $W_i$ of the components of $X_L$: localizing an affine ring at the nonzero elements of the integral base identifies its primes over $0$ with the primes of its generic fibre, so minimal such primes correspond to dominating components. Their generic fibres are geometrically irreducible by Step 1, and have dimension $d$: each reduced component of $X_L$ maps finitely and dominantly to the integral $X_K$ (on an affine chart its ring is a quotient of the finite algebra $A\otimes_K L$, and $A\otimes_K L$ is finite free over $A$ on a $K$-basis of $L$, hence flat; [lem-sc-flat-going-down] applied below a minimal prime forces its contraction to be the minimal prime $0$ of the domain $A$), so [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension] gives equality. Each $W_i$ is proper over $S_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]; its dimension is finite by the same dimension formula, since its function field is finitely generated over $L$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, reduced closures of generic components and the vertical components

proof.text: For $d\geq1$, apply [lem-trf-de-jong-geometrically-irreducible-tower] separately to each proper dominant $W_i\to S_0$. All its excellence, integrality, finite-dimension and geometric-irreducibility hypotheses were checked in Steps 2--3. Write its output as $b_i:T_i\to S_0$ and $h_i:P_i\to W_i$, where $P_i\to T_i$ is a tower of length $d$. If $d=0$, instead take $T_i=W_i$, $P_i=T_i$ and $h_i=1$: the generic fibre of $W_i\to S_0$ is a zero-dimensional integral finite-type scheme over $L$, hence a finite field spectrum by [lem-pc-dim-zero-finite-over-field]. Thus its generic fibre is finite and [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] makes $W_i\to S_0$ finite over a dense open. It is proper dominant, hence surjective, and so an alteration. The identity is the required length-zero tower.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, application of de Jong 5.9 and the parenthetical finite-morphism case

proof.text: Construct a common integral alteration $T\to S_0$ explicitly. Form the finite product $R=\prod_{S_0}T_i$. It is proper over $S_0$: each product projection is a base change of a proper $T_i\to S_0$, then use composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Its generic fibre is the spectrum of the tensor product over $L$ of finitely many nonzero finite field extensions. This tensor product is a nonzero finite-dimensional $L$-algebra (tensor products of nonzero finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field are nonzero). Choose one prime in it and take its reduced closure $T$ in $R$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Then $T$ is integral, proper over $S_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and dominates $S_0$. Its generic fibre is that single closed point, with residue field finite over $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] it is finite over a dense open, hence an alteration. Each projection gives $T\to T_i$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, sentence taking a common altered base; explicit finite-product construction

proof.text: The composite $a:T\to S_0\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], dominant and integral on sources. Its generic function-field extension is finite, so its generic fibre is finite: its nonempty affine charts have finite-type coordinate domains inside a finite extension of $K$, hence are finite-dimensional fields, and its irreducibility makes it a single point; [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] gives finiteness over a dense open of $S$. Thus $a$ is an alteration. The finite-type morphisms $T\to S_0\to S$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] make $T$ Noetherian. Excellence follows affine locally from [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Finally [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension], applied to $a$ with its finite function-field extension, gives $\dim T=\dim S$, so in particular $T$ has finite dimension.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1 / Lemma 3.3.2, the final integral altered base; Stacks 02JX

proof.text: Pull each tower back along $T\to T_i$ and write $Q_i=P_i\times_{T_i}T$. Each curve factor remains proper, flat and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its geometric fibre is a geometric fibre of the original curve, so connectedness, reducedness, pure dimension one and the ordinary-double-point condition persist, directly by their geometric definitions. Thus $Q_i\to T$ is again a tower of length $d$. The map $Q_i\to W_i\times_{S_0}T$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated]: its source is proper over $T$ by composition of the curve factors, and its target is separated over $T$. For length zero these statements hold for the identity tower.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, replacing the altered bases by a common one and pulling back the towers

proof.text: The image of $Q_i\to W_i\times_{S_0}T$ contains every point of its generic fibre over $T$. To check this before the final field extension, put $F_i=k(W_i)$, $E_i=k(T_i)$ and $H_i=k(P_i)$. The generic point of $P_i$ induces $F_i\otimes_L E_i\to H_i$. Its kernel is a minimal prime: $H_i$ is finite over $F_i$, the image is a field finite over $F_i$, and $F_i\otimes_LE_i$ is a finite-dimensional $F_i$-algebra. Geometric irreducibility of $(W_i)_L$ says there is just one minimal prime after this field change. Hence the generic point of the irreducible generic fibre of $(W_i)_{T_i}$ lies in the image. The map is proper, as in Step 7, so its image on that generic fibre is closed and therefore is the whole fibre. Surjectivity persists under the field extension $E_i\to k(T)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Consequently the closed image of $Q_i$ contains the entire dominating component of $(W_i)_T$. No assertion about its vertical components is used.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, the unique dominating component after base change; generic-field verification

proof.text: Set $Z=X\times_ST$. This is proper over $T$, hence Noetherian, and has finitely many components [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Let $V\subset Z$ be the reduced closed union of all components not dominating $T$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its structure map is proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Its image is closed and omits the generic point of integral $T$, hence is nowhere dense. The remaining components are precisely the closures of the components of $X_{k(T)}$, each covered by a $Q_i$ from Step 8. Put $P=(\coprod_i Q_i)\amalg V$. Its induced map $e:P\to Z$ is surjective by these two classes of components. It is proper: after every base change a closed subset of a finite disjoint union has image a finite union of closed images; finite type holds on the finitely many summands, and the diagonal is the disjoint union of their closed diagonals together with empty off-diagonal pieces. This checks properness directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2, adjoining all the vertical components and taking the finite disjoint union

proof.text: Supply the finite singular closed subscheme for every curve factor $q:C\to B$ in the pulled-back towers. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to this proper flat finitely presented nodal curve. It gives the first-Fitting closed subscheme $D=\operatorname{Sing}(q)\subset C$, supported exactly on the nonsmooth locus, with $D\to B$ unramified. The composite is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points], and therefore finite by [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite]. Choose this $D$. Its complement $C\setminus D$ is the relative smooth locus supplied by the same nodal-family statement, so $C\setminus D\to B$ is smooth over the base $B$. The geometric fibres are connected reduced schemes of pure dimension one by Step 7, and the ordinary double point condition is the stated completion at the maximal ideal of the geometric fibre local ring. These are precisely the current definition's curve clauses. This works even when $D$ is nonreduced. In conjunction with Step 9, the towers and $V$ make $P\to T$ exactly an almost plurinodal datum of [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Each tower has relative dimension $d$ (its length), while $V$ has nowhere dense image.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1, tower data; Stacks 0C59 and 0C5B (nodal families), 02LS (proper locally quasi-finite is finite)

proof.text: Take the augmented Cech nerve of $e:P\to Z$: $Y_n=P\times_Z\cdots\times_ZP$ with $n+1$ factors, faces omitting a coordinate and degeneracies repeating one. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] proves the simplicial identities: both sides of each identity select or repeat exactly the same coordinates. The degree-zero matching map is $e$, proper surjective by Step 9. For $n\geq1$ the matching object is $P^{n+1}_Z$: its compatible vertices are $n+1$ points of $P$ with common image in $Z$, and every higher face is uniquely the corresponding subtuple. This holds on morphisms from every test scheme, so the universal property makes the matching map an isomorphism. Thus $Y_\bullet\to Z$ is a proper hypercover and $Y_0=P$. The products must be over $Z=X_T$ to give this augmentation.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1, coskeleton argument after Lemma 3.3.2; explicit Cech construction over X_T

proof.text: Every $Y_n\to Z$ is proper, by induction on its number of factors using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. As $Z\to T$ is proper, each $Y_n\to T$ is proper, in particular of finite type. The Noetherian scheme $T$ is quasi-compact, so [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] gives a finite bound on the dimensions of its fibres, separately for each $n$. No common bound in $n$, and no bound by the original $d$, is claimed. Steps 6, 10 and 11 provide all the other clauses of the statement.

proof_origin.place: Online author PDF, Proposition 3.3.1 and Lemma 3.3.2, printed p. 9; archival PDF WANTED. Explicit common-base construction, generic-field check, singular subschemes and Cech matching calculation added by Q82.

lean.statement: theorem exists_plurinodal_proper_hypercover {S X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S] [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian S] [IsNoetherian X] (hS : IsExcellentScheme S) (hX : IsExcellentScheme X) (hdimS : topologicalKrullDim S < ⊤) (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim X < ⊤) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [IsDominant f] : ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (a : T ⟶ S) (_ : IsIntegral T) (_ : IsNoetherian T) (D : AlmostPlurinodalDatum T) (Y : SimplicialObject (Over (pullback f a))) (e : (Y.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))).left ≅ D.source), IsExcellentScheme T ∧ IsAlteration a ∧ IsProperHypercover Y ∧ e.hom ≫ D.morphism = (Y.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))).hom ≫ pullback.snd f a ∧ (∀ i : Fin D.count, ((D.towers i).length : WithBot ℕ∞) = topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber (genericPoint S))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, LocallyOfFiniteType ((Y.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))).hom ≫ pullback.snd f a) ∧ QuasiCompact ((Y.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))).hom ≫ pullback.snd f a) ∧ ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ t : T, topologicalKrullDim (((Y.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk n))).hom ≫ pullback.snd f a).fiber t) ≤ (b : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ topologicalKrullDim T = topologicalKrullDim S
